projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Duane Iossi was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: We are now talking to Duane, and this is Saturday, September 28th, and it is 25 minutes to 11:00. Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Okay. Now, that's -- that there is a copy of that. You can have that.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, can I have this, too? Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And where is this -- this dedication at?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It is -- it's already been done. It was done in 1996.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But it's 970 -- 970 West --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- __+ Harbor Boulevard. That's this.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. And this is picture number 2?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That's the name of all the ships on there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Okay. And then, like I said, this is USS Midway, of St. Lo. And the first ship sunk by kamikaze, which was right beside us. He was sunken. And it's going to be a museum ship, probably next July, right -- right back here.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And this is -- is a -- a snap of a cemetery, which we dedicated that in October '96. This -- all these -- all these men on here was killed in this -- on this one battle. This ship lost 252 men, which is missing on there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: See how they have -- And then, our ship is on here, because we didn't got sunked. __+ named on that one.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: You did get sunk?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No, we did not.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: You didn't? Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Here is me, like I say, when they unveiled that. Unveiled that.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And you may want -- that's -- that's by -- this is the ones on there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: This one here?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. That's -- that me, about the fourth one right in there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That's me there issuing that.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But here, listed all that -- all right in order. And that's the same thing again. And this is -- this is the ship that was sunk by kamikaze.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It was the one that sunk that -- __+ in St. Lo, but this is coming down at us.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: This aircraft?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. And -- __+ and we shot down the plane 50 feet behind me.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And then, 50 feet behind me.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Now, this is you when you first went into the service?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. That's -- that's the plane coming down. And this -- this is a piece of the motor --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- of that plane. I picked up --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- that's carrying pieces of the motor --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- of that plane I picked up.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But I -- I was now over here. The plane just --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Can I get a -- let me stop this. [Tape record shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. You were just saying that you --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: This is where we received our high school diploma on May the 19th, 19 -- 2001. 2002. I'm sorry. This is -- is the superintendent of the schools, and this is the school board president. And then, here is me and my brother, Edward, and the -- and ship and my -- us three. We received our diploma in -- in -- in -- in Alliance, Nebraska. Now, this is my granddaughter. Her birthday's today.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: She received her high school diploma the same year as I got mine.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, now, is that great or what?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: High -- put our high schools -- she got her diploma in 2001, and mine is dated 2001.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, that's neat. That is just really nice.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I don't know whether you want to put those in the book or not.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Sure. Absolutely.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: You can have those two.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Good. Thank you. Let me shut this off. [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. And you can just talk right in here. That's the microphone. And when we run out of tape, it will beep us. So -- then I've got another tape, so, we'll put it in there.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: So, go ahead.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I went to Farragut, Idaho, which is in northern Idaho, for boot camp August the 6th, 1943.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How old were you?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I was 18. I didn't finish my year in high school. That's why I got __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Veteran's Administration offered us our high school diploma. I went to boot camp in Farragut, Idaho about three months. Then we went to Bremerton, Washington, Seattle, Washington for additional training.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Where were you living at when you joined the service?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I was in Alliance, Nebraska.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And why did you decide you went into the -- Army? Navy. Excuse me. I'm sorry.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I went in -- I had -- was drafted -- it was drafted at the same time. Navy needed so many, and the Army, so many.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And then, they shipped us about a month later. We shipped up to Farragut, Idaho, and we did boat training on Lake Ponderay. Biggest ship -- biggest lake in the -- in the state. And I was there for about around three months. And I went to Birmingham, Washington, Tacoma, Washington for additional training. And December the 7th, 1943, I boarded the USS Fanshaw Bay, which is just a new ship just commissioned and the crew. And we worked on the ship and loaded up all of that. And then, we --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you were on board the ship, what would you say your job title was?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, we was all just load -- just -- I didn't have a job title then --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- unloading the freight.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And then, we went up to Ft. __. Additional loading of it. And then, when we came back down, we came at --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you were on board ship, what was the living conditions like, and the food?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It was very -- we -- I -- I can't complain about the food at all. Okay? We -- we -- we loaded -- we loaded the airpla- -- the ship, and they called it a cruise ship. Testing cruise. It was a dry run. We made a trip to Australia with an a load of P38s. Just test our ship.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you say "test the ship," do you mean just to see how much it would carry or how long it would take?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah, that's all.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: See the -- it just -- they do that to all ships, but that was our first trip out to Australia.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And what year was this?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: In '9 -- in January of '44.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And we did all the load P38s for __+ to Australia. And then, we made a stop at Farragut -- made a stop at -- oh, darn. Made a -- we went and made a __+ aboard the ship and made the -- came back to San Francisco and loaded up __+ across the equator. And fortunately, we went to Brisbane right after going to Australia, and I happened to get ahold of my brother. He was stationed in the Army there. So, he came aboard the ship to see me.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, that's nice. When you -- was it your first time away from home?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was that difficult for you?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Not really, no. Now, this is our route __ we travelled in. After we came back from San Francisco, we made several -- we traveled 150,000 miles. Our ship did and __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And we -- I was on that ship for about two years, as long as anybody else.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And this -- this was all of the -- all of the routes that you took?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That's all the routes we took.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How many were you on the ship?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Two years.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Two years?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. And I been to Japan three times, Hawaii several times. Here's Hawaii, you know.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And all this time, you were hauling freight back and forth?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, we was in action __.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. The first action I was in was Saipan, Mariana Island, which was June the 17th, 1944. And it was the longest continuous air attack then. About 90 Japanese __ dropping bombs. We're fortunate we only got one bomb and lost 17 men, which was unfortunate, I feel.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Were you afraid during all this attack?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No. Not really. It's a job. You didn't really --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: What did you do when you were being attacked? What was your -

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I was on the gun.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I was a gunner.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Shooting down those guys.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did you have any successful shots?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We -- I don't know.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: All of us had shells. We were there. About 20 of us shooting at one thing. You don't know who --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah. Exactly. That's true.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Just like this here, I got a suicide plane. I know I didn't shoot them down. We did.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Exactly. That's a good point.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: It was a team effort.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. The whole thing -- the whole ship was a team effort. I didn't do nothing spectacular. It's just a team effort.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How many men were on the ship?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Nine hundred and thirty, including the air groups.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And the average age -- I want to say about the average age was 21.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Who was your commander?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, we had several of them. Admiral Arnold, Admiral Cliffenspraig (ph), and Admiral -- Captain Johnson. We had several of them on the ship __.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. When you were in the service, were there any men friends that you made that you still communicate with today?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Very much so. Some of the men -- there was 20 of them that was on the ship that I knew real, real well.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Some -- two -- about four of us was in the same boot camp together --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- at 18 years old. And we all -- we all got together until --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And you're still friends?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Isn't that wonderful?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Comradery is great.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yes. Yes. And it had to make your living better to have friends.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I know.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Had to.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But we just looked forward -- we're already making plans for next year __+. We're going to be in San Francisco next year.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We're taking all the ocean crews up in San Francisco.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We're all working on that.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good. Good. Good. So, all this time when you were out -- when -- when you went out to sea, how many months at a time were you out to sea?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That's kind of a hard question. I'd say, probably the longest time -- we stopped at some of the islands, though. We brought some supplies on our ship. I'd say, maybe -- I think it was about six months was the longest we was out. That -- that length of time since I -- we was __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did you write back and forth to your family a lot?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Oh, yes. That's all I ever got done was writing letters.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did you?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How long would it take for you to -- if you sent a letter home to your mother, how long would it take before she got it and how long before --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I really don't know, really.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: No clue?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I'd say maybe 10 days.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, that's not too bad.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: That's not too bad.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And we stopped -- just like when we went to Australia with these loader planes. On the way back, we would stop in and there was a -- the mail bags there for us. The airplanes caught us a new -- we didn't get mail maybe -- It's hard to say. Maybe every -- every week, we got something.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you were in battle, were there days or many, many hours that you didn't sleep? What was it -- what was a day like if you were under attack?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, I'll say, when we first -- when we first were in the boarding ship in 1943, we loaded the ship of all supplies. And our day was 36 hours long. We did -- the only rest we got is if you go hide out somewhere. And then -- and then, they brought food over for us to eat. Normally, it wasn't -- because we had to get all the ship ready to go out and all.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But that was the longest day I put in for a long time.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: If you weren't on the guns, what did you do?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I took care of the life rafts, and I was -- I had to rig the lines so the men could go over to paint the side of the ship. I did that, and I spliced wire cables and __+ the boat.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When -- how long were you in the service again? I'm sorry.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It was a little over two-and-a-half years.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Two-and-a-half years?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you got out of the service, what did you do? Did you go right back home?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yes. I went right back home. Got discharged in St. Louis, and in -- in December of '45, we arrived in Nebraska there. And soon after, I got a job. I had to help take care of my mother. She was alone.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did you use your GI bill for any --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No. I -- at the time, I did. A lot of things I wish I would have did, but - --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Don't we all?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. I forgot about -- Yeah. I helped take care of -- I was the youngest one in the family, so I had -- in fact, I sent my mother half of my wages.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: What were your wages during that time?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: About 25 a month. Overpaid; wasn't we?

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did they -- when they paid you, did you have money in hand or did they put it in an account for you?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: They did have a payday come around. And we could either draw it out or draw -- well, these were all into a bank account, and then I didn't draw anyhow. Now, one time, I got a rate, and then I turned it down. And so, they overpaid me for three months. So, I had to pay all that back. So, I was getting a dollar a month there for about two months. There was nothing to spend money --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Cigarettes were a nickel apiece, and I never did smoke.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Cigarettes, a nickel a pack. __ are free. Cokes and ice cream was probably two or three cents. So, there was really nothing to spend on, but gambling out there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah. What kind of activities did you have when you were on board and when you went to shore?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, we, on the flight decks, we had a shuffle board, and then we had boxing matches there. Let's see.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, gosh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And then -- yeah. We had boxing matches, shuffle board, and weight lifting. And then, this is the basketball team we had on the -- And -- and __+ we tried entertainment, but __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: What kind of entertainers did you happen to see while you were over there?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, I'll tell you, I seen an awful lot. There was one right there. Oh, jeez. This is an Army show. I don't remember this, but they came aboard ship and put on a show for us, this crew. And then, I seen Bob -- this is -- we made our own entertainment.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, yeah? Guys dressed like women? [Laughter.] Had to have a good dance partner.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Oh, they was a good dancer. I'll tell you. And we had movies __. On the whole, I would say, 90 percent of the time, he was good.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: He wasn't extra good. He was good.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But it was our job. We had to do it.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And as far as I was concerned, I could probably take it down -- it's hard to say. Actual action on our ship, I could probably say maybe 10 total hours.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Well, that's good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. I mean, we was in the war zone all the time. But as far as actual -- actual -- now, the Battle of Leyte Gulf, it lasted for two-and-a-half hours. They would shoot down with 18-inch shells. We was just sitting ducks out there. And Saipan, we was -- that only lasted an hour. It happened to be the longest continuous air attack battle in history. Battles like that. There's a movie that's out now, Windtalkers.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, yes.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That was based on Saipan.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And when I went and seen the movie -- I have the date there. We was there June 16th, 1945 -- '44. And that -- but they didn't -- I was disappointed in the movie. They didn't do -- do us on the show, but that was based on Saipan.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Hmm.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Little Indians. I met two of them.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Hmm. That's neat.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And during the Battle of Leyte Gulf -- this is a big deal. It was the biggest sea battle in history. It involved -- it involved 13 ships. Now, I'm jumping ahead of myself again. The whole thing covered 100,000 square miles and we was taking it over the Philippines, which the United States had about 600 ships involved. We was clearing away from __ Land, which was -- which was -- which was October the 20th, '44. And then, break it down to our -- our group, 13. Now -- then it's called the Second Battle of the Philippine Sea. Then, the other battle __ was called Battle of Leyte Gulf. Then this one, which is our 13 ships __+, because it was unique, because we was the only one -- we had suicide plane coming down, we had 18-inch shells coming in at us from the other ships coming at us. That's why it was the biggest sea battle in history. We lost 895 men and 13 ships.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How -- how -- how long did the battle last?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It was about two-and-a-half hours.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And then, they -- thank God the Japanese turned around and left us. Another half hour, they could have got us all. Because they -- they had 18-inch shells, and the biggest gun we had, one and five inch. About that big around. We could -- they was 20 miles away. Our guns were only good for about a mile.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Like I said, you're just -- it was --it was a job. I can say.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you -- when you were on -- on your gun, when you were in a battle like this, you had to have been pumped full of adrenaline.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How did you stay focused?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- as a 19-year-old kid, we probably __ around. Nothing we could do. The gun I was on was a small gun. I couldn't do nothing. I just went to the __ good-bye. And what saved us, they used our __ shells, which they just went right on through. Now, going to this picture, this was the first ship sunk by shell fire, which is Gambier Bay, same -- same as that. That's -- this is just a painting.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: That's Gambier Bay?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: This is Gambier Bay.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Let me write that down.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It was the first ship sunk by kamikaze. Of course, this is a painting, but it --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And they shot at us with -- with colored shells. The reason they did -- it was just -- it was just like that. The reason they had them, the Japanese had the starter plane up above; would land and tell them where the shells was landing.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But our -- our -- our plane went up and got it down. But this is -- this -- right there, they was going around us like that there for two-and-a-half hours.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Man.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And the kids I talked to thought -- said, "That was real pretty; wasn't it?" It was -- it was pretty.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: That was pretty.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. Pretty and pretty bad.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Pretty evil.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But they -- thank God the Japanese turned around and left us. Thank God.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yep. Yep.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But like I said earlier there, I'd say 90 percent -- 80 percent of my time was good time in the Navy.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And as far as action __. And we -- we lost 40 men, which is not bad.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How did -- when you lost those 40 men, how did you bury them?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We buried them at -- we buried them at sea there. Yeah. Burial at sea there. They canvassed over at __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was there a regular ceremony that was --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. We had a regular __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: You had a chaplain and -- Now, is this your gun here? I know I'm getting -- this is one of the guns that you shot?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, this is it right here.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: This is -- this is a bigger gun, with a shell that long.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I lost a good buddy there.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How did it feel when you lost someone?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, you just had to turn around and go on and take his place.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: You know, you didn't -- you can't sit down and weep about it. I mean, it -- it gets you maybe the next day, what happened -- what happened yesterday. So, we had -- we buried 17 at one time __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was that pretty emotionally charged?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, it was kind of like a funeral now. It may not -- you may not know him. He's a ship mate, though.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Maybe -- I didn't lose any -- only lost two men I knew real well. Well, anyway, they -- they had the ramp. They put the flag, and you just slide -- just slide them over. So -- Am I taking too much of your time here?

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: No. You're fine. You're fine. Let me shut this off here a little bit.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. Okay. [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Were there many airplanes that crashed coming and going off your ship?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Oh, yeah. Seems like you had a crash all the time. And if they missed the barrier -- see, the cable is high here?

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And the other ones are about that height and that hook catches, but the next -- the wheel and -- crash into it.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And did this happen pretty often?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Actually, every time we was running a flight through there __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And how often was that?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We had -- we had a flight -- sometimes twice a day and sometimes it wasn't for a week or two.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: So, when they -- when they wrecked these planes, did you just push them off into the ocean?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: If they couldn't be repaired, you'd dump them off into the ocean. Most of them, we just pushed over __+.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was it -- when this happened, when they wrecked on those aircrafts, did they replace it, bring it in from another ship or --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, we did -- had them come in. Our ship help 30 -- 30 of them. There was __. Yeah, I was __.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did you get into boxing?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No. No. We -- shuffle board __+. There was always something to do. Playing cards and gambling was the biggest part of it.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was it?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Where -- where did they gamble at?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: You did it anywhere.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Anywhere? Anywhere you wanted to?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Anywhere you wanted to. Now, this is my group here.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: This is called the first division. Each one of those is a different division on the ship. Those guys are mostly gunners and --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: So, if -- if -- if you had all these divisions and you're gunners, what -- does each division have a separate job?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay. So, you guys -- the first division are the gunners?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: We have gunners and -- well, there's a gunner __ just repaired the guns.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But we was called the deck crew. Every time we'd land, we had to bring __ food on there. Here's a little history of our ship I got from the Navy department. But, yeah, that burial ceremony is kind of spectacular. I mean, they just __ buried at sea.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Did -- when you were in the service, when you came out, did it prepare you or change anything in your life?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Not really. I just grew up there. You're more an adult pretty fast.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you came home, what did you -- you went back home. And then, you just -- did you get married right away?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No. About five years after, I got married.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Was it?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. Just -- see, my family -- I was the youngest one in the family, and my brother was in the Army, and he -- he got out, though, before I did. But we all kind of worked together; helped my mother out. My mother and -- parents separated when I was 10 years old.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Kind of changed the pattern a little bit.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah. Was -- is there any stories that you'd like to share with me? Any special events that you have that --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No. I don't think. I think all of them are kind of special events. Nothing really -- nothing --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Nothing exceptional?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: No, nothing exceptional. Well, let's -- let's -- let's use this one here. Up on the __ in the ship -- this is called the __. The __ end of the ship, right here. Two guys got a big chunk of bee- -- beef and put it on the hook and __. And I went up there a little bit and I started helping him. He put a lightbulb on the line to shine on the meat, dropped it -- we was anchored there. A six-foot shark got ahold of that thing. We had one heck of a time pulling him up on the ship over there. I -- I wanted -- I thought he was dead. I wanted to get some of his teeth as souvenirs. The closer I got, I thought, he may want my arm first in there. But as of today, I'm damn sure we didn't finish killing that whale (sic), so I can get some teeth. But -- I mean, that was really something. I mean, normally, you're not fishing. Why we did that, I don't know.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Entertainment.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. But it -- we had a -- we had to hook up the anchor chain and pull -- pull the shark back up because it was heavy.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: When you went to -- when you were on leave, where did you go to?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Hung around -- I -- it had to be -- if I had a leave a week or two, then I went back to Nebraska to see my family.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But if I only had a day or two, we'd just get -- wherever we pulled in, anchored at. San Diego or Los Angeles or San Francisco.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: What did you do when you -- let's say you went to San Diego for a couple days. What did -- what did you do when you were there?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Well, it seemed like we always -- always ended up going to the USO. When we pulled into San Diego, we hitchhiked over to Los Angeles, then went down to the radio station and see the radio shows --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: How nice.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- and the __ Hall and -- and there was going to one -- one USS place, __ Hall and to -- Kay Kyser was playing __+. And I went back to the lunch counter to get me a sandwich. They lady fixed it all up, gave me the sandwich. She said, "Just a minute. I'll join you." That was Ma Kettle.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, really? Now, how neat that is.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I said, "The heck with dancing. I'm going to stay here and visit you."

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: So, I sat there about an hour just talking.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Nice person?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Oh --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, isn't that --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: I met so many people __. Bob Hope, met him. We seen his show twice __ Island.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And all -- we went to a lot of radio shows and big bands then. The biggest -- we had a big party. There was about 500 of us there. I don't know. Whoever put this party, they had all kinds of food for us. And Dick __ was a band -- played the band for us. And they was -- he was -- they was as drunk as everyone else.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: [Laughter.]

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And that was quite a deal. But like I said, I'd say 90 percent of the time, it was a good time.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, that's good.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: That's good. I want to -- [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: We're sitting here looking at the picture when his ship was bombed and he'll explain that -- what happened now.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yeah. We was on this here -- this -- this bomb landed from a Japanese plane up above. It made a hole about maybe 20 feet from me and blew up -- made the hole in the flight deck, right through. And we lost 17 men down there, which is the most we lost at one time.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: In the bottom deck?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: In the bottom deck, yeah.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: -- __, which is 158 ships. Now, ours was the one in yellow. When I say "ours," our group. We was called __ Cabbie Three.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: There was a Cabbie One, which was another group of ships, and Cabbie Two, which is another group of ships. Now, when these Kamikaze came, they hit this -- the Cabbie Two -- Two first, then us 10 minutes later. So, we wasn't the first. We was one of the first. The kamikaze __. Now, the one they got marked here were the ships we lost, in the black.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And -- and this is -- this is -- you going to make a copy of that?

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: This is the Philippine -- the Philippine -- this is the 13 ships here.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And on that paper there you got, it tells about the -- what the 13 ships are. Now, This is the second -- our second __ we got, and these are our air groups. B-68, they was with us, and they battled -- they have it listed as 124 days of action.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: A hundred and twenty-four days. And to tell you the truth, I can't recall that. I mean, we was in the battle zone all the time. Most of the time. Even right out of California, the Battle of __ battle zone. They was -- some reason, close to us.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But they -- they came up with 124 days. Now, part of that is, that one special air group in there __+ we -- we floated on Okinawa for 69 days, around and around the water. Didn't know whether we were going straight or in a circle.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: [Laughter.]

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But the main reason that special air group I pointed out to you earlier, they flew over the island to take pictures for the Army, and -- and that's part of the 129. And I can't do it. I can't come up with action 129 days, but it's there. And this is the one we got -- this is the one from the Philippines.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Our Philippine president __.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Now, that's -- this girl failed to -- it might have been my fault. __+ in there, the Philippine wasn't.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. Let's get some copies of -- [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: You were just saying you're the plank owner of --

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: USS Navy Gulf. And I'm an honorary plank owner -- I'm an honorary plank owner of the Navy Gulf CTs 55, and I'm a plank owner for the USS Fanshaw Bay, June the 9th, '43.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: And what does "plank owner" mean?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: It means, the first crew on the ship.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: The first crew and ship. Now, honorary wasn't the first crew. I was honorary, though. Now, here I am sitting in the captain's chair --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, that's neat.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: And the captain -- the captain of that ship, he says, "Is this your ship?" And I told him I was a plank owner. "You're a plank owner? I didn't know no one else was ever on that ship." I was the only one.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, great.

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: But he said, "It's your ship. Do what you want." We ate anywhere we wanted to and --

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Oh, great. That's great. [Tape recorder shut off.]

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Okay. You dedicated a time capsule?

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: Yes. In -- which was in 1994 in Pensacola, Florida. The cemetery there. The time capsule was six feet deep. And there was all kinds of pictures in there. In fact, this here. I got one of these books in there and a bunch of pictures __+. And that will be opened up in the year 1944. You're going to be around to open it up.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Hopefully. [Laughter.]

sp.speaker: Duane Iossi
sp.p: That's only 43 years later.

sp.speaker: Renaie Day
sp.p: Yeah. Hopefully, I'll still be kicking. Okay. Let's get copies of those. [END OF CD ONE.]
